report.experience: I finished the scene at canAdvance. The hungry household gave me a concrete entry point, and the shared limit on human control in Luther and Aquinas was the most worthwhile connection. The final distinction between the dead person and living buyer sharpened what might otherwise sound like a generic anti-payment message. I largely followed evident pairings rather than making difficult choices. The long inherited inventory was initially distracting; I have no lived experience of its earlier chapters. This logical text protocol cannot establish visual, touch, or human enjoyment.

report.experience: I made jam, syrup and marmalade and stopped at canAdvance. Jam was immediately legible; moving juice to the saucepan taught me how location unlocks combinations. Marmalade surprised me usefully with water before sugar. Having to move already cooked softened citrus back into the same saucepan felt like mechanical housekeeping. The sugar reading was specific and sober, but separate from the cooking actions. This logical interface cannot establish visual, touch or human enjoyment, and I did not experience the checkpoint history.
report.nextExperiment: Observe whether a fresh touch player independently stages juice at the saucepan and understands why softened citrus must be placed there again; ask what they expect before each move.
